items.title: AMC vs. Robinhood: Tokenized Stock Showdown
points: AMC CEO Adam Aron called Robinhood's stock tokens tracking AMC's share price "contemptible, outrageous, disgusting, detestable, inexcusable, vile," claiming they lack U.S. securities registration.
Aron says AMC has no connection to the tokens and has instructed outside securities counsel to investigate immediately.
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev faced similar pushback from OpenAI and SpaceX, which disclaimed involvement in their own tokenized versions.

Tenev plans to list "thousands" of private companies as tokenized stocks (digital tokens meant to track the price of shares without being the actual shares), with AMC explicitly included despite its CEO's objections.

items.title: Bitcoin Drops Below $80,000 on Strong Jobs Data
points: August U.S. payrolls came in at 162,000 jobs, nearly triple the forecast 53,000, reviving inflation concerns.
Federal Reserve September rate-hike odds rose to 58% from 49.4% following the report.
Bitcoin fell from a four-month high of $82,240 to below $80,000; prediction markets showed 52% odds it lands between $78K/$80K by September 6.
On the Myriad prediction platform, bets favoring bitcoin above $82K collapsed 87% in relative terms after the data release.

items.title: Trezor Data Breach Widens
points: An additional 67,000 Trezor hardware wallet customers were exposed in a widening data breach.
Some exposed records date back to 2019, far exceeding the company's stated 90-day data retention policy for partners.
The incident raises questions about third-party vendor data handling in the crypto hardware wallet ecosystem.

items.title: IMF Revises Stance on El Salvador's Bitcoin Holdings
points: The IMF (International Monetary Fund) now says donations funded the growth of El Salvador's Bitcoin reserves.
This reverses its year-old claim that reserves only shuffled between government wallets without real growth.

items.title: U.S. Bitcoin ETFs Post Best Day in 9 Months
points: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that let investors buy Bitcoin exposure through traditional stock markets) took in $730 million in inflows in a single day, the strongest since roughly December.
A major law enforcement organization dropped its opposition to the CLARITY Act, a bill aiming to set clearer U.S. rules for digital assets.
The reversal removes a political barrier that had complicated passage of the act and is seen as boosting institutional confidence in Bitcoin ETFs.

issues.subject: 🚀 U.S. Bitcoin ETFs Just Had Their Best Day in 9 Months

headlines: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs received $730 million in inflows as law enforcement dropped opposition to the CLARITY Act, marking the strongest single day in 9 months.
Major law enforcement group's reversal on cryptocurrency regulation removes a key political barrier to clearer digital asset rules.
Bitcoin ETF momentum accelerates as regulatory uncertainty decreases and institutional investor confidence strengthens.

sections.title: Law Enforcement Stance Shifts on CLARITY Act
points: A major law enforcement organization withdrew its opposition to the CLARITY Act, a significant political development for crypto regulation.
The reversal removes institutional resistance that had previously complicated passage of clearer cryptocurrency rules.
This support signals growing acceptance across traditionally skeptical government agencies toward explicit digital asset regulation.
